clue.text: Hit, and wound cruelly should be brought to book!

indicators.note: a cruel beating leaves things battered out of shape, so these letters are knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A violent assault demands that the culprit be brought to justice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cruelly' rearranges HIT plus WOUND; 'and' only joins. The definition plays on 'brought to book': a detective story is a book in which the criminal is brought to justice.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective novel is a book whose whole plot exists so the guilty party is caught and punished.

clue.text: Disregarding a railway engineer — with caution!

indicators.note: disregarding the letter a means it is set aside from the railway's letters
to engineer is to contrive or rework, so the remaining letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A railway engineer goes about the job very carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engineer' looks like a noun for a railwayman but is a verb asking for a rearrangement: RAILWAY without one A gives RILWAY, which 'engineer' turns into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting with caution means acting carefully and on guard against danger.

clue.text: Going beyond the limit, tread on someone's toes?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, off the end: past the edge of what is allowed
an idiom for causing upset or giving affront

explanation.definitionFit: Running off the end overshoots a limit; treading on someone's toes is hurting their feelings.

clue.text: Recollect her aunt — outwardly lovely but could be weird

indicators.note: read as re-collect, gathering the letters together again in a new arrangement
outwardly points to the outside of the word lovely, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Remembering an aunt who looked lovely but may have been rather strange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recollect' seems to mean remember, but read as re-collect it rearranges HER AUNT into UNEARTH; 'outwardly' takes L and Y, the first and last letters of 'lovely'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weird seems not of this world, eerie and supernatural.

clue.text: Long drawn-out surgery for mate in Berlin

indicators.note: surgery cuts things up and sews them back differently, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lengthy operation on a friend in a German hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surgery' rearranges MATE IN BERLIN; 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless or seemingly without end is tediously long drawn-out.

clue.text: Salt Scotsman spread on airport runway

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor, as is a tar
Mac is a stock name for a Scotsman, from the surname prefix

explanation.surface: A Scottish sailor at an airfield seems to be doing some resurfacing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salt' looks like seasoning but is the noun for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: The asphalt material laid on runways and roads is known by this trade name.

clue.text: For one, work may be play

definitions.text: For one, work may be play

parts.words: For one, work may be play
parts.note: for this person a job means appearing in a stage drama, so work and play are the same

explanation.walkthrough: The paradox of work being play resolves once 'play' is read as a stage drama.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage performer's paid employment consists of appearing in dramas.

clue.text: To avoid work by this ploy, am returning but dawdle

definitions.text: To avoid work by this ploy

indicators.note: returning means the word am is read backwards

parts.note: to dawdle is to linger

explanation.surface: Someone shirks a job by turning back and taking their time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reverses AM to give MA; 'but' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Feigning illness is the classic ploy for dodging one's duties.

clue.text: Exchange views? Quite the opposite!

definitions.meaning: as a noun, the reverse or contrary of something

explanation.definitionFit: To talk is to trade opinions with someone; as a noun the same word names a contrary proposition.

clue.text: Mulls over shows in reverse

definitions.meaning: what a mirror does, giving back a reversed image

explanation.definitionFit: One meaning is pondering something; the other is how a mirror gives back a back-to-front image.

clue.text: Heading north, something warm for the shoulders is taken

parts.note: a stole is a wrap worn round the shoulders

explanation.surface: Heading north, a traveller finds a warm wrap has been pinched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading' only links here: N for north is simply added after the wrap.
explanation.definitionFit: Taken here means pinched or carried off by a thief.

clue.text: Average simple chap pledges to be frugal

parts.note: par is the normal or average level
Simple Simon is the nursery-rhyme simpleton
IOUs are written pledges to repay a debt

explanation.surface: An ordinary, unsophisticated man promises to live thriftily.
explanation.walkthrough: Simple Simon is the foolish boy of the nursery rhyme; 'to be' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Being stingy and sparing with money is the core sense of both words.

clue.text: Vessel turning back about nothing

indicators.note: turning back means the pieces for about and nothing are read in reverse order

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
nil means nothing

explanation.surface: A ship turns round with nothing aboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' reverses the whole of RE plus NIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A large passenger ship on a regular route is a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Sort out the back row

parts.note: the rear is the back
a range is a row, as of mountains

explanation.surface: An instruction to tidy up the back row of a theatre or team photo.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things into a new order is to reorganise or sort them out.

clue.text: Fetters on donkeys restricting run! They are damaging their health

parts.note: fetters are chains

indicators.note: restricting means hemming in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: moke is British slang for a donkey
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Donkeys hobbled so they cannot run are suffering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'restricting' means holding in, so the run sits inside the donkeys; 'on' only links. Moke is old British slang for a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: People who light one cigarette from another are harming their own lungs.

clue.text: Heir's won battle with prince, for possession

indicators.note: a battle throws everything into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as the letters of heirs

explanation.surface: An heir has fought, alongside a prince, to keep the estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heir's' keeps its S as a letter here; 'battle' rearranges it with 'won', and 'with' and 'for' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Having title to something is possessing it.

clue.text: Is tide on turn? Impressions given!

indicators.note: a turn is a change of course, so these letters are put in a different order

explanation.surface: Wondering whether the tide is turning, someone gives their impressions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' rearranges IS TIDE ON; 'given' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A print run of a book or newspaper is a printing, an impression.

clue.text: Muses by the landing-stage on certain days

parts.note: a pier is a landing-stage for boats
the ides are particular dates in the Roman calendar, mid-month

explanation.surface: Poets find inspiration by the jetty on particular days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' only links the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The nine goddesses of the arts were named after Pieria, their haunt near Olympus.

clue.text: This line of work involves my riding afar

indicators.note: involves in its sense of entangling or twisting together, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer explains that the job means riding far afield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involves' rearranges MY RIDING AFAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping cows for milk is an occupation, a line of work.

clue.text: First aid required on beagle's tail bones

parts.note: stern is the hunting term for a hound's tail

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word aid

explanation.surface: A beagle hurt at the tail needs first aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First aid' is not a single phrase here: 'First' takes A from 'aid'. In hunting, a hound's tail is its stern.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural of the breastbone's anatomical name, so a set of bones.

clue.text: Title that gives you a good reputation

definitions.meaning: a right or claim, as in entitlement to recognition

definitions.text: that gives you a good reputation

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a rightful claim to recognition; the other is the esteem a person earns.

clue.text: Protective cover seaman rarely required

definitions.meaning: an archaic word for a sailor, hence rarely used

explanation.definitionFit: A tarred canvas sheet; in old usage the word also meant a sailor, so it rarely names one now.

clue.text: Strangely eager to be of one mind

indicators.note: strangely suggests the letters are behaving oddly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Oddly enthusiastic to share the same opinion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strangely' rearranges EAGER.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people who concur share a single opinion.

clue.text: It turns, recording on tape our religious leaders

indicators.note: leaders points to the first letters of the five words before it

explanation.surface: Our clergy's sermons are taped for broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'religious leaders' looks like clergy, but 'leaders' takes the first letter of each of the five words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotating part, as the blades of a helicopter, is something that spins.

clue.text: Given to soldiers but taken by clergymen

explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers receive commands; clergymen take holy orders when ordained.

clue.text: Under stress —— having taken the alternative, retired

indicators.note: having taken means holding inside, so one piece contains the other

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed
the other is the alternative

explanation.surface: Anxious after choosing the other option, someone went to bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' reads as an adjective but stands for being in bed; 'having taken' puts the alternative inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being flustered or worried is being under strain.

clue.text: Rest is ordered for woman in hospital

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A hospital patient is told to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' looks like a doctor's instruction but rearranges REST IS; a senior nurse is a sister in British hospitals.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals a senior nurse in charge of a ward has this title.

clue.text: Has to change schedule for first team, then stick with it

indicators.note: to change asks for these letters to be swapped round

parts.note: a plan is a schedule

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word team

explanation.surface: A manager changes the first-team plan, then decides to persevere with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges HAS into ASH; 'first' takes T from 'team'. 'then' and 'with it' only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A walking stick cut from an ash sapling.
